```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
```

## Introduction

This tiny project analyzes a **Movie Ticket Booking System** database using R.
The database contains customer, movie, theatre, show, seat, payment and booking information.

The analysis follows the basic R Markdown approach used in the reference project: importing a CSV file, displaying the data, checking its structure and missing values, performing summary statistics, creating frequency tables and visualizations, and studying relationships between numeric variables.

## 1. Import the Database

Keep this R Markdown file and the CSV database in the **same folder**.

```{r import-data}
movie_data <- read.csv(
  "Movie_Ticket_Booking_System_100_Rows.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

movie_data
```

## 2. Display First 10 Records

```{r first-rows}
head(movie_data, 10)
```

## 3. Number of Rows and Columns

```{r dimensions}
cat("Number of bookings:", nrow(movie_data), "\n")
cat("Number of variables:", ncol(movie_data), "\n")
```

## 4. Summary of the Database

```{r summary}
summary(movie_data)
```

## 5. Structure of the Database

```{r structure}
str(movie_data)
```

## 6. Check Missing Values

```{r missing-values}
colSums(is.na(movie_data))
```

## 7. Booking Status Analysis

```{r booking-status}
booking_status_count <- table(movie_data$Booking_Status)
booking_status_count
```

### Booking Status Pie Chart

```{r booking-status-pie}
pie(
  booking_status_count,
  main = "Booking Status Distribution",
  labels = paste(
    names(booking_status_count),
    booking_status_count
  )
)
```

## 8. Movie Genre Analysis

```{r genre}
genre_count <- table(movie_data$Genre)
genre_count
```

### Movie Genre Bar Chart

```{r genre-bar}
barplot(
  genre_count,
  main = "Movies by Genre",
  xlab = "Genre",
  ylab = "Number of Bookings",
  las = 2
)
```

## 9. City-wise Booking Analysis

```{r city}
city_count <- table(movie_data$City)
city_count
```

### City-wise Booking Bar Chart

```{r city-bar}
barplot(
  city_count,
  main = "Bookings by City",
  xlab = "City",
  ylab = "Number of Bookings",
  las = 2
)
```

## 10. Payment Method Analysis

```{r payment}
payment_count <- table(movie_data$Payment_Method)
payment_count
```

### Payment Method Pie Chart

```{r payment-pie}
pie(
  payment_count,
  main = "Payment Method Distribution",
  labels = paste(
    names(payment_count),
    payment_count
  )
)
```

## 11. Ticket Quantity Analysis

```{r ticket-quantity}
ticket_quantity_count <- table(movie_data$Ticket_Quantity)
ticket_quantity_count
```

### Ticket Quantity Bar Chart

```{r ticket-quantity-bar}
barplot(
  ticket_quantity_count,
  main = "Ticket Quantity Distribution",
  xlab = "Number of Tickets",
  ylab = "Number of Bookings"
)
```

## 12. Ticket Price Statistics

```{r ticket-price-statistics}
cat("Mean Ticket Price:", mean(movie_data$Ticket_Price), "\n")
cat("Median Ticket Price:", median(movie_data$Ticket_Price), "\n")
cat("Variance of Ticket Price:", var(movie_data$Ticket_Price), "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation of Ticket Price:", sd(movie_data$Ticket_Price), "\n")
```

## 13. Total Booking Amount Statistics

```{r total-amount-statistics}
cat("Mean Total Booking Amount:", mean(movie_data$Total_Amount), "\n")
cat("Median Total Booking Amount:", median(movie_data$Total_Amount), "\n")
cat("Minimum Total Booking Amount:", min(movie_data$Total_Amount), "\n")
cat("Maximum Total Booking Amount:", max(movie_data$Total_Amount), "\n")
```

## 14. Movie-wise Booking Analysis

```{r movie-bookings}
movie_count <- table(movie_data$Movie_Name)
movie_count
```

### Movie-wise Booking Bar Chart

```{r movie-bookings-bar}
barplot(
  movie_count,
  main = "Bookings by Movie",
  xlab = "Movie",
  ylab = "Number of Bookings",
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.7
)
```

## 15. Theatre-wise Booking Analysis

```{r theatre}
theatre_count <- table(movie_data$Theatre_Name)
theatre_count
```

### Theatre-wise Booking Bar Chart

```{r theatre-bar}
barplot(
  theatre_count,
  main = "Bookings by Theatre",
  xlab = "Theatre",
  ylab = "Number of Bookings",
  las = 2
)
```

## 16. Booking Status and Total Amount

```{r status-amount}
status_amount <- aggregate(
  Total_Amount ~ Booking_Status,
  data = movie_data,
  FUN = sum
)

status_amount
```

### Total Booking Amount by Status

```{r status-amount-bar}
barplot(
  status_amount$Total_Amount,
  names.arg = status_amount$Booking_Status,
  main = "Total Booking Amount by Booking Status",
  xlab = "Booking Status",
  ylab = "Total Amount"
)
```

## 17. Payment Method and Total Amount

```{r payment-amount}
payment_amount <- aggregate(
  Total_Amount ~ Payment_Method,
  data = movie_data,
  FUN = sum
)

payment_amount
```

### Payment Method Revenue Chart

```{r payment-amount-bar}
barplot(
  payment_amount$Total_Amount,
  names.arg = payment_amount$Payment_Method,
  main = "Total Booking Amount by Payment Method",
  xlab = "Payment Method",
  ylab = "Total Amount",
  las = 2
)
```

## 18. Correlation Between Ticket Quantity and Total Amount

```{r correlation}
correlation_value <- cor(
  movie_data$Ticket_Quantity,
  movie_data$Total_Amount
)

correlation_value
```

## 19. Ticket Quantity vs Total Amount

```{r scatter-plot}
plot(
  movie_data$Ticket_Quantity,
  movie_data$Total_Amount,
  main = "Ticket Quantity vs Total Booking Amount",
  xlab = "Ticket Quantity",
  ylab = "Total Booking Amount",
  pch = 19
)
```

## 20. Booking Analysis by Movie Genre

```{r genre-amount}
genre_amount <- aggregate(
  Total_Amount ~ Genre,
  data = movie_data,
  FUN = sum
)

genre_amount
```

### Genre-wise Total Booking Amount

```{r genre-amount-bar}
barplot(
  genre_amount$Total_Amount,
  names.arg = genre_amount$Genre,
  main = "Total Booking Amount by Genre",
  xlab = "Genre",
  ylab = "Total Booking Amount",
  las = 2
)
```

## 21. Key Results

```{r key-results}
cat("Total number of bookings:", nrow(movie_data), "\n")
cat("Total tickets booked:", sum(movie_data$Ticket_Quantity), "\n")
cat("Total booking amount:", sum(movie_data$Total_Amount), "\n")
cat("Average ticket price:", round(mean(movie_data$Ticket_Price), 2), "\n")
cat("Average booking amount:", round(mean(movie_data$Total_Amount), 2), "\n")
cat("Correlation between ticket quantity and total amount:",
    round(correlation_value, 3), "\n")
```

## Conclusion

The Movie Ticket Booking System database was successfully imported into R and analyzed using R programming.

The project demonstrates basic data analysis techniques such as data importing, data inspection, summary statistics, missing-value checking, frequency analysis, aggregation, correlation and graphical visualization.

The HTML report generated from this R Markdown file provides a clear presentation of the database analysis and can be used for a college-level R Programming Tiny Project.
